findings.evidence: With DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL unset — which is how an issue pod comes — `go test -run TestARoleRoutedEventTellsTheRoleLaneToKeepNothing ./internal/dispatch/outbox` prints `--- SKIP` under -v and `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/outbox 0.021s` without it. My first reading of this test at both heads was therefore vacuous and I nearly recorded it as pinning its fix when it had not run. findings.severity: observation, measured, for the architect to judge
findings.what: At a mid-drain handover the OLD holder keeps receiving for as long as the role claim takes to reach the listener's claim cache — about 220 ms in my run, 10 further copies.
findings.evidence: Live, 60 copies kept, receipts answered after 120 ms so the drain kept walking. B claimed while A had 11 copies; A ended with 21 and B took 39. From the listener log: A's last forward at 12:54:51.876612446Z, the drain's `listener kept role drain left the lane to the role's new holder` at 12:54:51.876674080Z — 62 MICROSECONDS later — and B's first forward 27 ms after that. So the drain is not lagging: it stops at the very first holder read that sees the new claim, exactly as designed (roleKeepDrainHolds reads CachedRoleHolder before every copy). What takes the time is the claim becoming visible in that cache. No copy reached both holders and none reached neither (60 of 60 delivered exactly once).
findings.why it matters: The architect's criterion reads `a claim by a second session mid-drain sends no further copy to the first`. Strictly, it does send a few — bounded by the claim-cache propagation window, not by the lane's length. Every message still reaches exactly one live holder, nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated, so I do not read this as a defect; but it is not literally zero and the criterion should say what it means before someone reads my pass as the stronger claim.
